reaction.episode: CORRECTION episode through the Nov 17 close: SPX 7,340.53, 6.42% below its 120-day high and 0.05% below its 200-day ($7,344.53); SMH $460.10 and NVDA $155.46 both below Zone 2; VIX 25.46 at the close, its 5-day high with no rollover; HY OAS 3.34 calm; mechanical tally 1 of 4 (only credit calm confirmed). Both stand-down lines tripped at the close.

reaction.trapRisk: The trap is a gap-up on the NVDA print while VIX is still above 25: NVDA was oversold at RSI 22.5 and the after-hours tape already bounced (QQQ snapshot $664.35 versus a $656.95 close, AVGO up 4.54%), so a relief gap is likely and can fail within days. Entries wait for VIX back under 25, the failure-zone retest verdict, and a second low that holds — never the gap-up open.

strategyPosture: Watch, with the stand-down in force. No new money: VIX closed at 25.46, above the 25 line, and SPX closed below its 200-day at 7,340.53 versus 7,344.53, so both stand-down triggers held into the close. Hold existing positions and do not average down in the leveraged names; the NVDA after-hours bounce changes nothing until it survives a regular-session close.

themes.counterRead: The stand-down now governs deployment, but it is a correction read, not a crisis read: credit is calm and the concentration block still reads ROTATION_NOT_ROLLOVER. The two tripped lines change what we buy (nothing, for now), not what we hold.
themes.dataAnchor: Both lines tripped at the close, not just intraday: VIX closed at 25.46, up 11.13% on the day and 47.08% over 20 days, its 5-day high with no rollover; SPX closed at 7,340.53, down 1.03% on the day and 4.82% over 20 days, 6.42% below its 120-day high and 0.05% below its 200-day ($7,344.53). HY OAS is 3.34, still calm and below the 4% line, and the mechanical tally is 1 of 4 (only credit calm confirmed).
themes.label: Stand-down lines tripped at the close

themes.watchFor: VIX close back under 25 and SPX close back above its 200-day $7,344.53; both lines must clear together to lift the stand-down.

NVDA is still roughly $20 below its $175 Zone 2 floor and SMH is below its $470 floor, so the bounce has to survive a regular session before it means anything — and a gap-up into the failure zone is the trap case the ladder already anticipates.

whereWaveBuilds: The next move builds off the NVDA print's digestion: a confirmed bounce (NVDA close above $175, SMH inside Zone 2 $470-505, VIX back under 25) opens a relief move toward the SPX failure zone $7,750-7,820, while a failed gap-up with VIX still above 25 starts the correction's next leg toward the 7,300 zone. FOMC minutes tomorrow (Nov 18) are the second trigger.
